title: How do they compare?
description: A picture lesson about comparative and superlative adjectives. 12 pictures in 4 groups show positive, comparative, and superlative forms (height, heat, crowds, suitcase weight). Written exercises cover completing sentences with comparatives and writing new sentences.
answer_note: Textbook written exercises and practice A/B are open-ended (suggested answers). Grammar answers are from the grammar practice book key.

lesson.text: Hans is the tallest student in our class.
The day before yesterday was the hottest day in the year.
There was a large crowd at the race last year.
This year the crowd is larger.
It is the largest crowd I have ever seen.
The blue suitcase is heavier than the brown one.
The green suitcase is the heaviest of them all.

lesson.title: Listen and describe the pictures
lesson.instruction: Look at the pictures and describe them using positive, comparative, and superlative forms.
lesson.translation: 看图并用原级、比较级和最高级形式描述它们。
lesson.answer_note: Model answers based on the pictures.
lesson.context: Each group of three pictures shows positive, comparative, and superlative forms.

questions.answer: Sophie is tall.

questions.prompt: Picture B: Sophie and Paul standing together
questions.answer: Paul is taller than Sophie.

questions.prompt: Picture C: Four students standing together
questions.answer: Hans is the tallest student in our class.

questions.prompt: Picture D: A sunny day at the beach (few people)
questions.answer: It is hot today.

questions.prompt: Picture E: A sunny day at the beach (more people)
questions.answer: It was hotter yesterday.

questions.prompt: Picture F: A very crowded beach (many people)
questions.answer: The day before yesterday was the hottest day in the year.

questions.prompt: Picture G: A race with a large crowd watching
questions.answer: There was a large crowd at the race last year.

questions.prompt: Picture H: A race with an even larger crowd
questions.answer: This year the crowd is larger.

questions.prompt: Picture I: A race with the largest crowd
questions.answer: It is the largest crowd I have ever seen.

questions.prompt: Picture J: A brown suitcase on a scale
questions.answer: The brown suitcase is heavy.

questions.prompt: Picture K: A blue suitcase on a scale (heavier)
questions.answer: The blue suitcase is heavier than the brown one.

questions.prompt: Picture L: A green suitcase on a scale (heaviest)
questions.answer: The green suitcase is the heaviest of them all.

lesson.title: Written exercises A: Complete sentences with comparatives
lesson.instruction: Look at these words: cold—colder; nice—nicer; hot—hotter; heavy—heavier. Now complete these sentences. Example: It is warm today, but it was warmer yesterday.
lesson.translation: 注意这些形容词的比较级形式：cold—colder; nice—nicer; hot—hotter; heavy—heavier。模仿例句完成以下句子。
lesson.answer_note: Model answers completing sentences with appropriate comparative forms.
lesson.context: Complete each sentence with the comparative form of the adjective.

questions.prompt: Example: It is warm today, but it was ________ yesterday.
questions.answer: It is warm today, but it was warmer yesterday.

questions.prompt: It is cool today, but it was ________ yesterday.
questions.answer: It is cool today, but it was cooler yesterday.

questions.prompt: It is wet today, but it was ________ yesterday.
questions.answer: It is wet today, but it was wetter yesterday.

questions.prompt: He's late again today, but he was ________ yesterday.
questions.answer: He's late again today, but he was later yesterday.

questions.prompt: This test is easy, but that one is ________.
questions.answer: This test is easy, but that one is easier.

questions.prompt: This bookcase is large, but that one is ________.
questions.answer: This bookcase is large, but that one is larger.

lesson.title: Written exercises B: Write new sentences with comparative and superlative
lesson.instruction: Write new sentences. Example: I am very young. → I am younger than you are. I am the youngest in the class.
lesson.translation: 模仿例句改写以下句子，写出比较级和最高级形式。例句：我非常年轻。→ 我比你年轻。我是班上最年轻的。
lesson.answer_note: Model answers writing comparative and superlative sentences.
lesson.context: Write two sentences for each adjective: one with the comparative and one with the superlative.

questions.answer: I am younger than you are. I am the youngest in the class.
I am older than you are. I am the oldest in the class.
I am taller than you are. I am the tallest in the class.
I am lazier than you are. I am the laziest in the class.
I am heavier than you are. I am the heaviest in the class.
I am luckier than you are. I am the luckiest in the class.
I am fatter than you are. I am the fattest in the class.
I am thinner than you are. I am the thinnest in the class.
I am bigger than you are. I am the biggest in the class.

lesson.title: Written exercises C: Write new sentences with comparative and superlative
lesson.instruction: Write new sentences. Example: This policeman is tall. → But that policeman is taller. He is the tallest policeman I have ever seen.
lesson.translation: 模仿例句改写以下句子，写出比较级和最高级形式。例句：这个警察很高。→ 但那个警察更高。他是我见过的最高的警察。
lesson.answer_note: Model answers writing comparative and superlative sentences.
lesson.context: Write two sentences for each: one with the comparative and one with the superlative.

questions.answer: But that policeman is taller. He is the tallest policeman I have ever seen.
But that street is cleaner. It is the cleanest street I have ever seen.
But that man is older. He is the oldest man I have ever seen.
But that river is longer. It is the longest river I have ever seen.
But that woman is shorter. She is the shortest woman I have ever seen.
But that knife is blunter. It is the bluntest knife I have ever seen.
But that car is cheaper. It is the cheapest car I have ever seen.

practice.title: Practice A: Polly is taller than John
practice.instruction: Look at this table showing comparative and superlative forms. Now compare these. Example: John—tall, Polly—taller, George—tallest of all → John is tall, but Polly is taller than John, and George is the tallest of them all.
practice.translation: 请看下表，注意比较级和最高级形式。完成以下句子。例句：John—tall, Polly—taller, George—tallest of all → John很高，但Polly比John高，George是他们中间最高的。
practice.answer_note: Model answers combining sentences with positive, comparative, and superlative forms.
practice.context: Combine each set of three statements into one sentence using positive, comparative, and superlative forms. Item 1 is a printed example.

questions.answer: John is tall, but Polly is taller than John, and George is the tallest of them all.

questions.prompt: this skirt—pretty, that one—prettier, the red one—prettiest in the shop
questions.answer: This skirt is pretty, but that one is prettier, and the red one is the prettiest in the shop.

questions.prompt: Mary is lucky, Ken—luckier, Tom—luckiest person I know
questions.answer: Mary is lucky, but Ken is luckier, and Tom is the luckiest person I know.

questions.prompt: the French test—easy, Maths test—easier, English test—easiest we've had for a long time
questions.answer: The French test was easy, but the Maths test was easier, and the English test was the easiest we've had for a long time.

questions.prompt: Paul had a low mark, Sophie—lower mark, poor Hans—lowest mark in the class
questions.answer: Paul had a low mark, but Sophie had a lower mark, and poor Hans had the lowest mark in the class.

questions.prompt: last summer—hot, the summer before that—hotter, this summer—hottest we've had for a long time
questions.answer: Last summer was hot, but the summer before that was hotter, and this summer is the hottest we've had for a long time.

practice.title: Practice B: About you
practice.instruction: Answer these questions with short answers or complete sentences.
practice.translation: 用简短形式或完整句子回答以下问题。
practice.answer_note: Open-ended personal questions. Model answers provided.
practice.context: Answer each question about yourself using comparative or superlative forms.

questions.prompt: Who is older— you or your friend?
questions.answer: I am older than my friend.

questions.prompt: Who is taller— you or your friend?
questions.answer: My friend is taller than me.

questions.prompt: Who is the cleverest person you know?
questions.answer: The cleverest person I know is my grandfather.

questions.prompt: Which are usually the hottest and coldest months in your part of China?
questions.answer: The hottest month is usually July and the coldest month is usually February.

grammar.title: Grammar I: Make sentences according to the example
grammar.instruction: Make sentences according to the example. Example: red car / blue car / white car fast → The red car is fast, the blue car is faster, and the white car is the fastest I've ever seen.
grammar.translation: 仿照例句造句。例句：red car / blue car / white car fast → 红色的车很快，蓝色的车更快，白色的车是我见过的最快的。
grammar.key_source: pdf/新概念英语语法练习1_按课程索引.pdf (Lesson 108 I, PDF p.539-540)
grammar.context: Make three sentences for each set: positive, comparative, and superlative. Item 1 is a printed example.

questions.prompt: red car / blue car / white car — fast
questions.answer: The red car is fast, the blue car is faster, and the white car is the fastest I've ever seen.
The men are happy, the women are happier, and the children are the happiest of all the people.
Sam's suitcase is heavy, Ann's suitcase is heavier, and Jack's (suitcase) is the heaviest of all the suitcases.
Jane is tall, David is taller, and Tony is the tallest in the class.
My shoes are small, your shoes are smaller, and her shoes are the smallest of all the shoes.
The dress is cheap, the shoes are cheaper, and the hat is the cheapest in the shop.
This watch is nice, that watch is nicer, and the blue watch is the nicest I've ever seen.
The white bird is big, the black bird is bigger, and the black and white bird is the biggest I've ever seen.

questions.prompt: Summer Palace / Imperial Palace / Great Wall — great
questions.answer: The Summer Palace is great, the Imperial Palace is greater, and the Great Wall is the greatest I've ever seen.
This carpet is lovely, that carpet is lovelier, and the carpet in the living room is the loveliest in the house.

grammar.title: Grammar II: Make dialogues according to the example
grammar.instruction: Make dialogues according to the example. Example: oranges / sweet → Those oranges are sweet, aren't they? Yes, they are, but these are sweeter.
grammar.translation: 仿照例句编对话。例句：oranges / sweet → 那些橙子很甜，是吗？是的，但这些更甜。
grammar.key_source: pdf/新概念英语语法练习1_按课程索引.pdf (Lesson 108 II, PDF p.540)
grammar.context: Make a dialogue for each pair using a question tag and a comparative response. Item 1 is a printed example.

questions.answer: Those oranges are sweet, aren't they? Yes, they are, but these are sweeter.
Those apples are big, aren't they? Yes, they are, but these are bigger.
Those tomatoes are fresh, aren't they? Yes, they are, but these are fresher.
Those peaches are nice, aren't they? Yes, they are, but these are nicer.
Those dresses are smart, aren't they? Yes, they are, but these are smarter.
Those eggs are large, aren't they? Yes, they are, but these are larger.
